claims.text: A computational method based on density functional theory with phonon-dispersion calculations can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed method is suitable for identifying materials for thermal-insulation applications.
Applying DFT with phonon-dispersion calculations characterizes phonon dispersion and lattice dynamics in high-entropy alloys.
Ab initio calculations provide detailed insight into phonon behavior.
Ab initio calculations provide detailed insight into thermal conductivity.
The proposed method will predict low-phonon-thermal-conductivity high-entropy alloys more accurately than current prediction methods.
The method's applicability is limited to high-entropy alloys and thermal-insulation applications.
Computational resource constraints limit the applicability of the proposed method.
The exact improvement in prediction accuracy is uncertain.
The method's performance across diverse high-entropy-alloy compositions is uncertain.
A comparative benchmark should evaluate the proposed method and current prediction methods on high-entropy alloys with experimentally known thermal-conductivity properties.
The benchmark should measure prediction accuracy and computational resource requirements.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant accuracy improvement over current methods would falsify the hypothesis.
Computational requirements that are prohibitively high for practical use would falsify the hypothesis.
